<p>The Veeva Vault Architect serves as the technical and strategic leader for designing, implementing and optimizing Veeva Vault solutions across the global organization.  This role ensures that all Vault applications align with business objectives, regulatory requirements, and enterprise architecture standards.  The architect collaborates closely with business stakeholders, IT teams and implementation / support partners to deliver scalable, compliant and high performing Vault-based solutions.</p>

<p><em>Integration &amp; Data Management</em><br>•    Architect and oversee integrations using native Veeva Vault Integrations, Veeva APIs, Vault Loader and middleware tools across both Vault and other applications.<br>•    Ensure adherence to data governance, master data strategies and cross system data flows.<br>•    Ensure data integrity, auditability, and traceability across the Vault ecosystem.</p>
<p><em>Stakeholder Collaboration</em><br>•    Work with business process owners to understand needs and translate them into technical solutions.<br>•    Collaborate with QA/SA, Compliance, Data Privacy and Validation teams to ensure system readiness.<br>•    Provide technical guidance to internal teams and external implementation partners.</p>

<p><em>Education</em></p>
<p>Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in computer science, information systems, engineering or related fields required. Veeva Vault certification(s) preferred.</p>
<p><em>Technical Skills</em><br>•    8+ years of experience in the configuration, implementation, support and operations of Veeva Vault-based solutions.<br>•    Proven expertise across multiple functional domains (Quality, Regulatory, Medical, Commercial and/or Clinical).<br>•    Hands-on experience with Veeva APIs, integration patterns and data migration tools.<br>•    Knowledge of GxP compliance, validation practices and regulated system requirements.<br>•    Experience with large-scale, global implementations.<br>•    Experience with middleware platforms (e.g., MuleSoft, Informatica), Master Data Management concepts and solutions preferred.</p>

<ul>

<li>Work closely with leadership to inform long-term commercial strategies and investment decisions.</li>

Based in Japan with worldwide operations, we work across the continuum from drug discovery to commercialization, guided by our commitment to patients and their families.</p>
<p>Our research teams, located in California and around the world, are focused on developing the next generation of antibody, cell, and gene therapies, with particular emphasis on bone and mineral disorders, hemato-oncology, and rare diseases. We accelerate development through collaborations with industry, academia, patients, and healthcare providers, and since 2018 we have introduced four new therapies serving patients with progressive illnesses often in need of new therapeutic alternatives.</p>
<p>Our culture is grounded in our values: <em>Commitment to Life</em>, <em>Integrity</em>, <em>Innovation</em>, and <em>Teamwork/Wa</em>, and brought to life through the Kabegoe Principles, which define the behaviors and actions that guide how we work together to deliver meaningful impact for patients.</p>
<p>We’re proud of the progress we’ve made and mindful of the countless individuals still waiting for their own breakthroughs. A commitment to making people smile unites our efforts. Learn more at <a href="http://www.kkna.kyowakirin.com">www.kkna.kyowakirin.com</a>.</p>
<p><strong>Summary:</strong></p>
<p>The Principle I, GRA-CMC is responsible for providing site-based global regulatory CMC leadership and support for the Sanford manufacturing facility. The role serves as the primary interface between the Sanford site and the global GRA-CMC organization, ensuring that site regulatory activities are aligned with global regulatory strategy, applicable requirements, and business priorities.</p>
<p>The role is responsible for regulatory activities associated with the FDA PreCheck pilot program and the Sanford Type V DMF, as well as providing GRA-CMC representation for site technology transfer activities. The position also provides regulatory CMC support to address the evolving regulatory requirements of the Sanford site and development pipeline.</p>
<p><strong>Essential Functions:</strong></p>
<p>•    Serve as the primary GRA-CMC interface for the Sanford site, providing regulatory CMC leadership, strategic guidance, and oversight to ensure site activities are aligned with global regulatory strategies, applicable requirements, and company standards.<br>•    Direct GRA-CMC activities associated with the FDA PreCheck program, including preparation for FDA interactions, regulatory communications, responses to agency requests, and associated follow-up activities.<br>•    Own the preparation, submission, and lifecycle management of the Sanford Type V DMF, ensuring that content remains accurate, current, and aligned with applicable regulatory requirements and product development and manufacturing activities.<br>•    Represent GRA-CMC within Sanford technology transfer activities, ensuring regulatory requirements, filing considerations, and regulatory commitments are identified early and appropriately incorporated into technical strategies and execution plans.<br>•    Assess regulatory CMC implications of Sanford site changes and manufacturing activities, including facility readiness, process and equipment changes, technical initiatives, and other site-related activities with potential regulatory impact.<br>•    Establish and maintain effective partnerships with Sanford Quality, Manufacturing, MSAT, Supply Chain, and other technical functions, as well as global GRA-CMC and development teams, to ensure timely identification, assessment, and resolution of regulatory CMC matters.<br>•    Proactively identify and evaluate regulatory CMC risks, developing appropriate mitigation strategies to support compliant and timely execution of site and development activities.<br>•    Contribute to regulatory submissions and health authority interactions for products manufactured or planned to be manufactured at Sanford, including assessment of CMC information, responses to regulatory questions, and other activities as required.<br>•    Shape regulatory CMC input into site and product lifecycle planning, including assessment of regulatory implications associated with manufacturing strategy, process changes, product introductions, and other business or development initiatives.<br>•    Support Sanford regulatory inspection readiness and execution, as applicable, including preparation for regulatory inspections, participation in inspection activities, and development of responses and remediation plans related to CMC matters.<br>•    Monitor and coordinate regulatory commitments and CMC actions associated with Sanford activities, working with relevant stakeholders to support timely and compliant completion.<br>•    Contribute to broader GRA-CMC post-approval maintenance activities and portfolio priorities, adapting support as business needs, regulatory requirements, and development priorities evolve</p>
<p><strong>Requirements:</strong></p>
<p><em>Education</em><br>Bachelor’s degree  in a relevant scientific discipline, such as Pharmacy, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, or closely related field. Advanced degree (M.S., Pharm.D., Ph.D., or equivalent) preferred, particularly in a pharmaceutical, scientific, or regulatory discipline.</p>
<p><em>Experience</em><br>•    Minimum eight (8) years of progressive regulatory affairs experience within the biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or life sciences industry, with substantial focus on CMC regulatory affairs.<br>•    Proven track record supporting U.S. BLA post-approval activities and lifecycle management; exposure to regulatory activities in other major markets (e.g., EU, UK, and ROW) preferred.<br>•    Demonstrated success managing complex regulatory CMC activities and projects across multiple functions, including site, technical, quality, manufacturing, and global regulatory organizations.<br>•    Prior involvement in FDA interactions and health authority engagements, including preparation of regulatory materials, responses to agency questions, and follow-up activities.<br>•    Background in manufacturing site regulatory activities, including technology transfers, manufacturing changes, facility readiness, and evaluation of regulatory impact.<br>•    Hands-on involvement in the preparation, submission, and/or maintenance of Type V DMFs or other CMC regulatory dossiers strongly preferred.<br>•    Demonstrated application of regulatory strategy and sound judgment to identify risks, evaluate options, and develop practical approaches to complex CMC issues.<br>•    Track record of working effectively within a matrixed organization and influencing outcomes across site-based and global functions without direct authority.</p>
<p><em>Technical Skills</em><br>•    In-depth knowledge of U.S. FDA biopharmaceutical CMC regulatory requirements, including expectations for development, manufacturing, post-approval changes, technology transfer, and lifecycle management.<br>•    Strong understanding of the FDA PreCheck Pilot Program and its regulatory framework, including the role of early FDA engagement, facility information, Type V DMFs, pre-operational reviews, facility readiness, and subsequent application and inspection activities.<br>•    Proficiency in CMC regulatory submissions and documentation, including BLA-related CMC content, post-approval supplements, Type V DMFs, regulatory responses, and supporting technical documentation.<br>•    Regulatory strategy and analytical capabilities to evaluate CMC regulatory risks, interpret complex technical information, and develop practical, risk-based recommendations.<br>•    Advanced regulatory writing and presentation capabilities, with the ability to communicate complex scientific and regulatory concepts clearly to technical, site, senior leadership, and health authority audiences.<br>•    Cross-functional communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build alignment, influence decision-making, and effectively communicate regulatory strategy and risk across site and global functions.<br>•    Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook; familiarity with electronic regulatory submission and document management systems preferred.<br>•    Familiarity with electronic regulatory submission and document management systems and other tools used to prepare, track, and maintain regulatory documentation preferred.prepare, track, and maintain regulatory documentation preferred.</p>
<p><strong>Non-Technical Skills</strong><br>Demonstrated ability to organize, prioritize, meet deadlines, make decisions, and change course of action quickly. Strong work ethic is required. Detail oriented and excellent follow through. Has the ability to flex and deal with ambiguity in a dynamic, fast-paced, high growth environment. Has a passion for personal learning and development to be able to grow with the company. Cultural sensitivity and ability to develop consensus within a multinational organization.</p>

In North America, we are headquartered in Princeton, NJ, with offices in California, Massachusetts, and Ontario</p>
<h3>Summary of Job</h3>
<p class="isSelectedEnd"></p>
<p data-pm-slice="1 1 []">The Senior Medical Science Liaison (MSL) will help shape how Kyowa Kirin’s Rare Disease Medical Affairs team engages with healthcare professionals, researchers, and investigators across South Central. In this field-based role, you’ll lead scientific exchange, bring insights from the field into medical strategy, and support research and education. You’ll have the opportunity to own your territory plan, lead field medical initiatives, and mentor fellow MSLs.</p>
<p><strong>Territory</strong>: Dallas, TX; Houston, TX; Phoenix, AZ; and surrounding markets. Candidates must live within the assigned territory. Travel is up to 70%.</p>
<hr data-start="1222" data-end="1225">
<h3 data-section-id="1peydm1" data-start="1227" data-end="1250">Essential Functions</h3>
<p></p>
<p></p>
<ul data-spread="false" data-pm-slice="3 3 []">
<li>
<p>Develop and execute a strategic territory plan that uses scientific and stakeholder insights to prioritize engagements, address unmet medical needs, and guide field medical activities.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Build and maintain trusted scientific relationships with healthcare professionals, key opinion leaders, researchers, and investigators across the territory and, as appropriate, nationally and internationally. Serve as a regional scientific resource by connecting stakeholders with relevant Kyowa Kirin resources and research collaborations.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Provide timely, accurate, balanced, and evidence-based information on disease states, treatment options, emerging clinical evidence, and Kyowa Kirin products. Respond to unsolicited medical information requests in accordance with company policy.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Gather and analyze field insights on unmet medical needs, treatment trends, and the competitive landscape. Translate those insights into recommendations for Medical Affairs strategy, scientific education, and evidence generation.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Develop and deliver scientific presentations, educational programs, and resources for external stakeholders and internal teams. Support speaker identification, development, and training as appropriate.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Serve as the scientific liaison for unsolicited investigator-initiated study proposals and ongoing studies. Partner with Clinical Operations and other internal teams to support company-sponsored studies as appropriate.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Lead field medical activities and provide scientific support at regional, national, and international congresses, advisory boards, investigator meetings, and other scientific forums.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Lead or contribute to Medical Affairs initiatives, strategic planning, and cross-functional projects. Mentor fellow MSLs by sharing scientific expertise, field insights, and best practices.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Maintain expertise through regular review of clinical literature, treatment guidelines, and emerging evidence. Communicate relevant product safety information in accordance with applicable requirements and company policies.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Collaborate across functions while maintaining appropriate boundaries between scientific and commercial activities. Participate in medical and promotional review as required, and conduct all activities in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, industry codes, and company policies, including pharmacovigilance and privacy requirements.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p></p>
<p> </p>
<hr data-start="4051" data-end="4054">
<h3 data-section-id="g9ewcs" data-start="4056" data-end="4069">Education</h3>
<ul>
<li>
<p data-pm-slice="1 1 []">Advanced clinical or scientific degree or healthcare professional credential required (e.g., MD, DO, PhD, PharmD, NP, PA, MS, or equivalent). Doctoral degree (MD, DO, PhD, or PharmD) preferred.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<h3 data-section-id="1n71tnc" data-start="4168" data-end="4182">Experience</h3>
<p></p>
<ul>
<li>A minimum of three years of Medical Science Liaison (MSL) experience in the pharmaceutical industry is required.</li>
<li>Experience supporting Rare Disease, Endocrinology, Metabolic Bone Disease, Nephrology, Rheumatology, or a related therapeutic area is strongly preferred.</li>
</ul>
<p> </p>
<p></p>
<h3 data-pm-slice="1 3 []">Skills and Competencies</h3>
<ul data-spread="false">
<li>
<p>Ability to critically evaluate medical literature, interpret clinical trial data, and communicate complex scientific information clearly and accurately to healthcare professionals, investigators, and internal teams.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Knowledge of clinical research methods and evidence generation, with the ability to stay current on disease states, treatment guidelines, standards of care, and emerging science.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Ability to build trusted scientific relationships across a geographically dispersed territory and translate field insights into recommendations that inform Medical Affairs strategy.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Ability to manage field activities independently, prioritize competing demands, solve problems, and exercise sound judgment as needs change.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Strong communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to influence without authority, work effectively across functions, and lead initiatives or mentor colleagues.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Working knowledge of FDA regulations, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), pharmacovigilance requirements, Office of Inspector General (OIG) guidance, and applicable industry standards.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Experience with Medical Affairs systems and customer relationship management (CRM) platforms, and proficiency in Microsoft Office.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<p> </p>
<h3 data-section-id="ewa2rj" data-start="5555" data-end="5580">Physical Requirements</h3>
<p data-pm-slice="1 1 []">The role requires the ability to work in a field-based environment with frequent travel, including extended periods of sitting during air, ground, and other forms of transportation. The position may require prolonged use of computers and other office equipment, as well as the ability to attend and participate in scientific meetings, conferences, advisory boards, and healthcare professional engagements. The employee must be able to navigate various work environments and maintain effective communication and presentation capabilities while traveling and performing job responsibilities.</p>
<h3 data-section-id="b6ss1z" data-start="5716" data-end="5738">Working Conditions</h3>
<p data-pm-slice="1 1 []">Field-based position requiring up to 70% travel by air and ground transportation, including overnight travel and occasional weekend commitments to support scientific congresses, advisory boards, and other Medical Affairs activities. Must reside within the assigned territory and maintain proximity to a major airport to support regional coverage requirements, which may encompass a broad geographic area requiring regular travel. A valid driver’s license and the ability to operate a motor vehicle as required for business travel are required.</p>
